root_cause.text: The uacce driver's vm_operations_struct lacked an explicit .mremap handler, causing the kernel to use the default mremap behavior which copies vm_private_data to the new VMA, leading to double-free of the queue resource (q->qfr) when both the original and remapped VMAs are unmapped.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states that "when the driver does not implement .mremap, it uses the default mremap method" which "copies the original vma's vm_private_data (i.e., q) to the new vma, both munmap operations would trigger vma_close, causing q->qfr to be freed twice." The patch adds a .mremap handler that returns -EPERM to prevent this scenario, and the fix is applied to uacce_vm_ops which previously only had a .close handler defined.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent remapping of uacce device memory regions by adding an explicit mremap handler that denies the operation.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `uacce_vma_mremap()` that returns `-EPERM`, and registered it as the `.mremap` callback in the `uacce_vm_ops` vm_operations_struct.
intent_record.how: This change prevents userspace from remapping (via mremap syscall) memory regions that were mapped through the uacce device. When a process attempts to remap such a VMA, the kernel will now invoke this callback and return -EPERM (Operation not permitted), blocking the remap operation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in this initial commit. The `uacce_vm_ops` structure (lines 313-315) defines only a `.close` handler (`uacce_vma_close`) but lacks an explicit `.mremap` handler. This causes the kernel to use the default mremap behavior which copies `vm_private_data` to the new VMA. The `vm_private_data` field is set to the queue pointer `q` (line 330: `vma->vm_private_data = q;`), and the queue contains a reference to `qfr` (queue file region) that is freed in `uacce_vma_close` (line 309: `kfree(qfr);`). When a VMA is remapped without a custom `.mremap` handler, both the original and new VMAs will have the same `vm_private_data` pointing to the same queue. When either VMA is unmapped, `uacce_vma_close` will be called and attempt to free the same `qfr` resource, leading to a double-free vulnerability. The fix would require adding a `.mremap` handler to the `vm_operations_struct` that prevents the default behavior or properly handles the remapping, but no such handler is present in this commit.
